## Observed Facts

- **Data Scope:** BGL dataset, all time (2005-06-03 to 2006-01-04), level = FATAL, grouped by node. Total FATAL Log Entries: 855,195 [E1][E2].
- **The top node is dominant.** R30-M0-N9-C:J16-U01 has 152,229 FATAL Log Entries, about 17.8% of all FATAL entries [E1].
- **The top 5 nodes together** have 156,732 FATAL Log Entries, about 18.3% of the total [E1]:

| Rank | Node | FATAL Log Entries | Share of all FATAL |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | R30-M0-N9-C:J16-U01 | 152,229 | ~17.8% |
| 2 | R71-M0-N4-C:J14-U01 | 1,567 | ~0.2% |
| 3 | R12-M0-N0-C:J12-U01 | 1,385 | ~0.2% |
| 4 | R03-M1-NF-C:J07-U01 | 966 | ~0.1% |
| 5 | R36-M1-N0-C:J16-U11 | 585 | ~0.1% |

 [E1]

- **The problem is concentrated on one node, not on a few.** Ranks 2–5 are an order of magnitude smaller than rank 1 (each under 1,600 entries) [E1].
- **Beyond the top 5, the FATAL volume is spread widely.** The grouping returned 31,481 distinct nodes [E1]. Ranks 6–50 each have roughly 300–435 entries, and most are I/O-type nodes (`-I:J18-`) across racks R00, R02, R03, R22 [E1]. This is a broad, low-per-node pattern rather than a hotspot.

## Hypotheses

- R30-M0-N9-C:J16-U01 is a single faulty or misbehaving node that is generating repeated FATAL messages. Its volume is roughly 100× the next node, so it likely accounts for most of the FATAL count on its own.
- The many I/O nodes at ~300 entries each suggest a second, systemic pattern (for example, a shared rack, midplane, or service condition) that affects many nodes at a low rate. This is a guess from the node names; the counts alone don't show the cause.

## Unknowns

- The counts do not show whether the 152,229 entries on R30 come from one event repeating or from many separate failures. They also don't show whether that volume is recent or spread over the period. A trend query on the time range would settle that.
- The logs don't show what the FATAL messages say on R30, so I can't name the failure type from these counts.
- These are Log Entries, not incidents. I can't say how many distinct failures produced them.
- I did not break down FATAL by component or alert_tag, so I can't say whether the R30 volume and the I/O-node pattern share a cause.

## Next Step

Start with R30-M0-N9-C:J16-U01. Pull a day-level trend and a sample of its FATAL messages to see whether the 152,229 entries are one repeating fault or many. Then run `count_by` on FATAL with `group_by=component` and `alert_tag` to check whether the ~300-per-node I/O pattern shares a cause with it.
